detailed_rationale:
Kalpataru Projects International (formerly Kalpataru Power Transmission) is India's largest power transmission & distribution EPC player, now diversified into buildings, roads, oil & gas pipelines, and a meaningfully sized international book (Nordics, South America, Africa, Middle East). FY26 was a genuinely strong year on every operating metric: consolidated revenue grew 22% YoY to Rs 271.43 bn, and profit before tax before exceptional items grew 62% YoY to Rs 13.34 bn -- margin expansion, not just topline growth. Q4 revenue alone was Rs 77.78 bn (+10% YoY).

The order book is the standout feature: FY26 order inflows totalled Rs 264 bn, taking the consolidated order book to Rs 654.57 bn as of March 2026 -- roughly 2.4x annual revenue, which gives multi-year revenue visibility that is unusually strong for an EPC business. International diversification is real and growing: the T&D business alone booked ~Rs 130 bn of order inflow in FY26 with 65% from outside India, and the company is currently L1 (lowest bidder, pending award) on roughly Rs 3,200 cr of further international work including a ~Rs 2,000 cr solar EPC project.

The balance sheet carries the working-capital intensity typical of large EPC contractors -- D/E of 0.46 and interest coverage of only ~3.5x, both thinner than a typical Ionic quality name, reflecting mobilisation advances, retention money, and receivables cycles rather than a structural solvency concern, but still a real sensitivity if execution slows or working-capital cycles lengthen. At ~22x earnings, the valuation is not cheap, but it is not unreasonable set against a 2.4x order-book-to-revenue ratio and margin expansion that is already showing up in the PBT growth rate.
recommendation_rationale: Already a quant-Hold; the exceptionally strong order book and margin trajectory are genuinely positive but do not offset the EPC sector's inherent working-capital/execution leverage (interest cover of only ~3.5x) enough to argue for anything beyond Hold at the current valuation.
summary: Kalpataru Projects International is one of India's largest power-transmission EPC contractors, now well diversified internationally and into other infrastructure verticals. Both revenue and profit grew strongly this year, and the order book -- at more than double annual revenue -- gives unusually good visibility into future work. The balance sheet carries the typical working-capital intensity of large contractors, which is a normal feature of the business rather than a new risk. We rate this a Hold: strong execution and a well-stocked order book, but the valuation already reflects much of that strength.
positive_para: Order book of Rs 654.57 bn is roughly 2.4x annual revenue, providing multi-year visibility that is rare in the EPC sector. FY26 profit before exceptional items grew 62% YoY -- well ahead of the already-strong 22% revenue growth -- showing genuine margin improvement, and the international order book (T&D orders 65% ex-India) provides diversification away from single-country policy risk.
negative_para: Interest coverage of only ~3.5x and D/E of 0.46 reflect the working-capital-heavy nature of large EPC contracting (mobilisation advances, retention money, long receivables cycles) -- a normal feature of the business but a real sensitivity if execution slows or if international project payment cycles lengthen. EPC margins can also be volatile project-to-project; the 62% PBT growth rate is unlikely to repeat every year.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~22x earnings, the market is crediting both continued double-digit revenue growth (supported by the 2.4x order-book cover) and sustained margin expansion. Given the order book is real and verifiable, this is closer to fair value than rich, but it already prices in a good execution outcome -- there is limited room for margin disappointment.
